````
# Web UI surfaces

Read [DESIGN.md](../../../DESIGN.md) before selecting page structure or controls.
It owns app layout and display conventions, including custom action pages.

## Find the current boundary

Apply [discovery reuse](../carta-module-development/SKILL.md#discovery-reuse).
Start with the changed route/resource or generated source and the applicable
reference below. Reuse the plan's verified adapter and component choices.
Inspect an export or one nearby example only for an unresolved contract.
Before writing each new interaction pattern, identify its View or form, input
renderers, display renderers, value contract, action owner, and visible parent.
For custom reads or writes, read the
[query-cache contract](../carta-module-development/references/web-query-cache.md).
Identify the loading owner and every data consumer affected by a write.
Read [Fields](references/fields.md) for every resource display and
[File routing](references/file-routing.md) for every child section.
Discovery is complete when each visible field names its table value and its detail value,
and each interaction has supported configuration, route placement, loading and
refresh ownership, or a named framework gap. Keep these
decisions in the existing work record and reuse them for matching interactions.

Read `docs/architecture/web-application-architecture.md` when ownership or app
integration is unclear; use `docs/ui/README.md` for technical UI references.
Inspect `apps/web/src/main.ts`, app defaults or the authenticated layout only
when changing their setup or resolving a registration/default problem. Read
the navigation manifest when adding an entry. Keep framework changes within scope.

## Framework-first composition

Use established framework patterns directly. Select the highest-level component
that supports the required interaction, including its states and feedback.
Before adding custom UI behavior, check the relevant component contract and
extension points. Use supported slots, fields, actions and framework controls;
keep custom code limited to the unmet requirement.

Select in order: standard View/action, supported slot or adjacent section,
lower-level framework component, then local code for a named unmet requirement.
Apply [action placement](../../../DESIGN.md#actions-and-forms). Check existing
examples against the design rules before reusing their composition.
Import template components or identify their runtime registration; a test stub
or type declaration does not register a component.

Check composition once per interaction pattern. Standard work records only a
real deviation in its work document; it needs no UI JSON. Use the
[UI contract](references/ui-contract.md) for full-process work, an existing
contract or custom composition that needs static checking. Review deviations
against the required result, not merely whether a slot supports them.

## Choose and build

| Work | Read |
| --- | --- |
| New page, app shell, navigation, visual hierarchy, responsive layout | [App conventions](references/app-conventions.md) |
| File routes, navigation entries, nested parents, tabs, Back, route lifecycle | [File routing](references/file-routing.md) |
| Lists, cards, filters, actions, dialogs | [Surfaces](references/surfaces.md) |
| Workflow detail, history, related records | [Detail layout](references/detail-layout.md) |
| Value contract for any new or changed relation, display field, or label | [Fields](references/fields.md) |
| Any user input, including custom actions and inline uploads; read before selecting controls | [Build resource forms](../build-resource-form/SKILL.md) |

Routes own URLs, query state, navigation, dialogs, and workflow feedback.
Schemas own data validation. A resource owns standard actions and one shared
field catalog. Pass the returned action directly to its View:

```vue
<ListView v-bind="records.list()" />
<DetailView v-bind="records.detail({ id })" />
<FormView v-bind="records.create()" />
<FormView v-bind="records.update({ id })" />
```

Use `createHonoResourceActions(rpc.<module>)` for standard transport. It already
normalizes responses. Keep custom transport in app actions. For custom resource
actions, use the [action contract](references/surfaces.md#custom-resource-actions).
Routes do not call raw RPC endpoints.
A file or wrapper earns its place when it owns behavior; simple standard
resources can call the adapter directly without a separate actions file.

## Check the result

Use [verification](references/verification.md). Report visible behavior checked,
failed checks, and any unverified result. Reuse the parent module's evidence;
do not start a second verification process.
````

```
1: # Cross-layer contracts
2: 
3: The approved design owns business behavior. The layer skills own code and UI
4: patterns. Use this file to check the boundaries between them.
5: 
6: - **Scope:** Select list, detail, create, update and delete independently.
7:   Implement the actions the product needs.
8: - **Names:** Keep persisted fields, API schemas, actions and resource fields
9:   aligned. Use the same domain labels across pages, validation and workflows.
10: - **Values:** Read [frontend-field-contract.md](frontend-field-contract.md) for
11:   display, draft and submit values, relation identities, assets and multi
12:   selections. Change schema, persistence mapping and consumers together.
13: - **Relations:** The API returns named relation objects for display and accepts
14:   the declared write key. Load the display shape on list, detail and returned
15:   writes. The server checks reference existence, access and parent membership.
16:   A filtered lookup is user assistance, not authorization.
17: - **Files:** Shared API storage owns upload, download and deletion. Distinguish
18:   a retained upload, external URL and owned child row in the data contract.
19:   Use the current public asset schemas and projection in `apps/api/src/storage`;
20:   reuse the web asset adapter. Keep module-specific upload routes, URL builders
21:   and compatibility value mappers out of ordinary resource code.
22: - **Queries:** The resource owner defines list filters and detail identity.
23:   Consumers pass parameters through the existing actions. Multi-selection query
24:   arrays use JSON and the API `selectionQuery(itemSchema)` contract.
25: - **Resource identity:** Use a required `string | number` record key, a nonempty
26:   tuple of distinct such keys, or a function returning a scalar or nonempty flat
27:   object of scalars. The default `id` must meet the same key rule. Runtime
28:   numbers must be finite; `0` and `''` are valid. Pass the declared identity
29:   shape to routes, writes and keyed invalidation; use `invalidate()` for all records.
30: - **Access:** Bind one permission policy across API, resource actions, route
31:   guards, navigation and seed data. Read the
32:   [API permission rules](../../api-conventions/SKILL.md).
33:   Server checks remain required even when the UI hides an action.
34: - **Backend routes:** Use the [file-routing contract](../../api-conventions/references/file-routing.md).
35:   Plan the inherited scope chain with each HTTP action.
36: - **Navigation:** Register each intended entry point in the app navigation
37:   manifest. A filesystem route alone does not add a sidebar entry.
38: - **State:** Specify deletion, recovery and workflow effects as observable
39:   behavior. Coupled writes that must succeed together use one transaction.
40: - **Freshness:** Read [web-query-cache.md](web-query-cache.md) for cached reads
41:   and invalidation of affected consumers after a mutation.
42: - **UI:** Use `$web-ui-surfaces` for page and navigation conventions and
43:   `$build-resource-form` for forms. Their visual defaults permit local choices;
44:   data contracts and accessible interaction remain requirements.
45: - **Proof:** Use [verification-strategy.md](verification-strategy.md). Test the
46:   behavior at its owner, then the integration where layers can disagree.
```

```
1: # Verification strategy
2: 
3: Verify the requested result with the smallest useful non-browser checks.
4: The original request and later decisions govern behavior. Optional refinements
5: are not completion gates.
6: 
7: ## Browser journeys
8: 
9: E2E is outside Carta module delivery. This applies to design, planning,
10: implementation, review, full-process work and resumed work, for
11: standard CRUD and custom workflows alike. Do not generate, write, run or repair
12: browser tests. Do not prepare browser test environments, collect browser reports,
13: assign journey IDs, or require a manual browser walkthrough as a substitute.
14: Do not run aggregate commands that start browser tests.
15: 
16: Browser testing requires a separate, explicitly requested task. Existing
17: framework tests remain unchanged. Move old browser obligations to that separate
18: scope; preserve their history and do not mark them passed. Missing E2E is not a
19: module defect or a completion blocker. Report actual UI behavior as unverified.
20: 
21: ## Select proof by behavior and impact
22: 
23: Use focused type checking and linting for changed owners. Add or run a small
24: schema/API test only for a module-specific risk not covered by current evidence.
25: 
26: | Risk | Useful proof |
27: |---|---|
28: | Validation | Accepted and rejected values through the actual schema. |
29: | Relation | API identity and returned label; source review of list/detail display and edit loading. |
30: | Access | Allowed reads and denied writes, with stored data unchanged on rejection. |
31: | Filter | API results for distinguishing records; source review of field/filter wiring. |
32: | Workflow | Legal/illegal transitions and coupled stored effects or rollback. |
33: | UI composition | Source review of fields, dependencies, relation labels, routes and standard actions. |
34: | Migration | SQL review and relevant existing-data checks on an authorized isolated target. |
35: | External integration | Current evidence for the actual provider contract, using a limited live check where needed. |
36: 
37: Source review does not prove rendered behavior. Record that limit without
38: starting browser work. Prepare the authorized development migration, seed and
39: preview URL as soon as viable under [execution](execution.md#prepare-and-build).
40: Do not wait for final test completion to make the preview available.
41: 
42: ## External integrations
43: 
44: Before building dependent behavior, identify unverified request and response
45: contracts. Use current evidence for the specified provider, model or version,
46: input format and options, or run a limited live check through the application
47: operation. A compatibility claim or a response invented for a mock does not
48: verify the external contract.
49: 
50: Resolve live-check authority early from the request and existing permissions.
51: If authority is missing, ask for the specific check, data and cost or request
52: limit while continuing independent work. Available credentials alone do not
53: grant authority. Use authorized test data, bound time and usage, and stop when
54: the required evidence is obtained or the agreed limit is reached. Report failures
55: and the next useful check before further paid retries.
56: 
57: Record the target, relevant request options and observed result without secrets
58: or sensitive payloads. Where useful, preserve a response with sensitive data
59: removed as a fixture for a stable regression test. Use local tests for malformed
60: responses, timeouts and error handling; distinguish technical failure from a
61: valid negative business result. A live connection check proves compatibility,
62: not model accuracy. Check accuracy with representative cases when required by
63: the requested outcome.
64: 
65: Keep a required integration with missing evidence visibly unverified. It prevents
66: completion: use REWORK for missing proof within authority, or BLOCKED when
67: authority or the environment prevents the check.
68: 
69: ## Test ownership
70: 
71: Trust established framework contracts for unchanged controls. Do not rediscover
72: their coverage for each field or repeat lookup, calendar, reset, readiness,
73: overlay and focus tests in modules. Framework gaps are separate work.
74: Module tests own schemas, relation sources, field dependencies, authorization,
75: business rules and persistence. Use actual module owners, not copied schemas.
76: 
77: Application integration is a separate boundary from unchanged framework behavior.
78: When local code coordinates submit, component lifetime, refresh or invalidation,
79: use a focused non-browser check that exercises that coordination through its
80: actual owners. Include write failure and successful write followed by refresh
81: failure where those paths differ. Keep source review for layout and configuration;
82: avoid tests that only repeat their text.
83: 
84: ## Test justification
85: 
86: Before adding a test, identify the plausible wrong result and the coverage gap.
87: Extend an existing suitable test first. No test-count target or new ledger.
88: Avoid snapshots, source-text tests, exact copy, field order and copied config
89: assertions unless these are explicit product contracts.
90: 
91: ## Tests that earn their cost
92: 
93: Assert public results and stored effects, not status alone. Use only fixtures
94: that distinguish the fault. Give them unique identities and clean up owned rows
95: after failure too. Keep related steps in one test when their sequence matters.
96: Do not mock the authorization or persistence boundary being claimed.
97: For regressions, demonstrate the intended failure when practical.
98: 
99: ## Commands and environment
100: 
101: Inspect current scripts and focused selectors once.
102: 
103: Use guarded isolated API test targets, never a development database for test
104: reset. Serialize checks that share mutable data and memory-heavy type checks.
105: Zero selected tests and skipped cases are not passes. Report exact blockers.
106: 
107: ## Test order
108: 
109: Use test-first work for regressions and critical access/data-loss rules when
110: practical. Routine routes and forms can precede their focused checks.
111: Do not change approved product behavior to satisfy a test.
112: 
113: ## Tight loop
114: 
115: Run a focused check after a meaningful boundary change. Preserve its output,
116: exact command and real exit status; a pipe can hide failure. Read saved output
117: instead of rerunning only to see another part. Classify failures as source,
118: test, fixture, environment, tooling or requirement.
119: 
120: After two failed attempts at the same fault, report the evidence, proposed cause
121: and next different check. If that check does not establish the cause, stop that
122: repair and request focused diagnosis; continue independent work.
123: Reuse current passes when their source, fixtures and environment remain valid.
124: A new reviewer or report format does not require another run.
125: Shared API tests use migrated schema and clean up only owned rows. A test that
126: replaces schema needs its own isolated target.
127: 
128: ## Evidence interface
129: 
130: Keep commands, exit status, selected cases, source state and non-secret target
131: identity in the existing work record. No recorder JSON is needed for ordinary
132: work. Record source-review findings and unverified UI behavior separately.
133: 
134: Support each required outcome with a relevant assertion or specific source-review
135: finding. Read the assertion before claiming coverage. An aggregate test count or
136: a type-check pass does not establish behavior outside its checks. Keep missing
137: required proof open even when all executed commands pass.
138: 
139: For the full process, select only API/UNIT evidence. Use the existing recorder
140: through `node scripts/module-evidence.mjs --help`. Include actual source, tests,
141: fixtures, config, lockfile, affected dependencies and approved design as inputs,
142: including dirty/untracked files. Keep reports outside the input set. Do not edit
143: old reports or remove inputs to make stale evidence pass. Document-only changes
144: need requirement review, not automatic runtime reruns, unless consumed at runtime.
145: 
146: ## Verdicts
147: 
148: - `PASS`: in-scope non-browser checks and source review are sufficient; required
149:   development setup is complete. State that browser behavior was not verified.
150: - `REWORK`: an in-scope defect or missing non-browser proof needs correction.
151: - `BLOCKED`: a decision, authority or environment prevents in-scope completion.
152: 
153: Separate defects and material proof gaps from optional suggestions. Do not waive
154: security, data protection or requested behavior to save time. Do not expand
155: verification into browser work to close a stated UI verification limit.
```

````
1: # Frontend field and input contract
2: 
3: Read this reference before a Carta web resource or form edit. The framework
4: owns the normal input behavior. A module declares only its domain difference.
5: 
6: ## Public field shape
7: 
8: ```ts
9: {
10:   label,
11:   display: { read?, renderer?, props?, format? },
12:   table: { ... },
13:   detail: { ... },
14:   form: { renderer?, props?, source?, validate?, write?, behavior? },
15: }
16: ```
17: 
18: - If `display.read` is absent, display reads `record[field.key]`.
19: - If `form.write` is absent, submit keeps the control value unchanged.
20: - Do not add `(value) => value` or an identity display reader.
21: - There is no public top-level field `read` or `write`.
22: - Field `form.validate` replaces the renderer's default non-empty control-shape
23:   validation.
24: 
25: ## Value and validation flow
26: 
27: ```text
28: loaded API value
29:   -> framework prepares the control value
30:   -> live control draft
31:   -> input default or form.validate
32:   -> form.write, when present, on a shallow submit copy
33:   -> resource schema
34:   -> action business validators
35: ```
36: 
37: Field authors do not configure another load or write path. The framework owns
38: the loaded-value preparation, and `form.write` remains the only field writer.
39: 
40: The framework runs field writers before the submit callback or resource
41: action. Submit callbacks and actions send their input unchanged. They do not
42: run a full-payload writer. Readiness checks inspect control values and do not
43: write them.
44: 
45: For a nested custom form block that has a non-asset submit conversion, put one
46: writer on the owning top-level field. Do not also write its child fields or
47: write the block again during submit. For assets, use the
48: [asset field contract](#asset-fields).
49: 
50: The live draft always keeps the control value. A writer is pure, changes only
51: its field on the submit copy, and never replaces a preview or selected record
52: in the live draft.
53: 
54: The input contract owns basic non-empty control shape:
55: 
56: - `number`: a finite JavaScript number;
57: - `file` and `image`: the [asset field contract](#asset-fields);
58: - `lookup` or `select` with `multi: true`: an array of exact selection record
59:   objects from the field schema. The schema must use
60:   `selectionValues(itemSchema)`; the framework rejects a missing or different
61:   schema and rejects `form.write`.
62: 
63: Empty values go to the resource schema. The resource schema owns requiredness
64: and the final submitted shape. Use action validators only for extra business
65: rules. For example, a number renderer already rejects text; use
66: `form.validate` only to replace that rule with a domain rule such as 1–15.
67: 
68: Built-in override parameters follow the renderer value type. An arbitrary custom
69: renderer receives `unknown` until its own contract narrows it. Check current
70: exports before relying on a planned type change.
71: 
72: ## Objects and identifiers
73: 
74: Do not apply one identifier rule to all inputs:
75: 
76: - A database-backed single relation keeps its scalar ID or code as the write
77:   field. The API also returns the named relation object for display, and
78:   `display.read` reads its label. Do not fetch only to label it.
79: - A lookup field keeps the source resource identity separate from its `pick` and
80:   `view` keys. Use the source identity for detail, CRUD, and cache operations.
81:   When a pre-filled value uses a different picked key, load it through a loader
82:   that accepts that key or through returned list records. Never pass `pick` as a
83:   detail ID. Review the actual form's load wiring and relation source. Do not
84:   add a browser journey for the lookup.
85: - A multi lookup or select keeps the exact selected records in the live draft
86:   and sends them unchanged. The backend extracts identity fields only at the
87:   persistence boundary, then sends current labels in the same record array.
88:   Do not map these values to IDs and do not add a field writer.
89: 
90: ## Asset fields
91: 
92: Use the same field name and asset shape in API reads, the live form draft and
93: submitted writes. A single field contains `StoredAsset` (or `null` when allowed);
94: a multi field contains `StoredAsset[]`. Preserve every asset property, including
95: optional metadata. Array position carries UI order. Framework controls add no
96: category, row identity or ordering property to an asset.
97:
````

````
Read 1/1 file, 104 lines
1: # Backend file routing
2: 
3: ## Ownership
4: 
5: `apps/api/src/routes` owns HTTP locations. Each `+server.ts` exports named HTTP
6: methods. Directories supply URL segments; `(group)` adds no segment; `[id]`
7: supplies a parameter. A default `defineScope(...)` export in `+scope.ts` applies
8: to that directory and its descendants.
9: 
10: ```text
11: routes/
12:   +scope.ts                         identity resolver
13:   health/+server.ts                 GET /health
14:   (authenticated)/
15:     +scope.ts                       session guard
16:     roles/
17:       +scope.ts                     entity and shared record conversion
18:       list/+server.ts               GET /roles/list
19:       detail/[id]/+server.ts         GET /roles/detail/:id
20: ```
21: 
22: Keep request context, identity, entity, shared authorization, and hooks in the
23: scope that owns their descendants. Keep operation permission and persistence
24: choices in the route. Ordinary helper and service files do not create routes.
25: 
26: Database domains remain explicit in `apps/api/src/domains.ts`. Permissions and
27: web navigation have separate owners. Adding a route requires no route registry.
28: 
29: ## Authoring
30: 
31: Developers must be able to add, move, or delete a route without knowing generation
32: exists. Use normal project commands and public package imports. Context, identity,
33: entity, and parameters must infer from the file tree: no generated imports,
34: manual generation, per-route type plumbing, or registry edits.
35: 
36: A move can change both URL and inherited access. Check the old and new parent
37: chains and affected consumers. Preserve existing URLs unless the requested
38: behavior changes them. A public SDK import owns consumer types; clients do not
39: import backend source files or private artifacts.
40: 
41: These complete files use the existing role entity:
42: 
43: ```ts
44: // routes/(authenticated)/roles/+scope.ts
45: import { defineScope } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
46: import { role } from '../../roles/roles.entity'
47: 
48: export default defineScope({ entity: role })
49: ```
50: 
51: ```ts
52: // routes/(authenticated)/roles/list/+server.ts
53: import { list } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
54: import { requirePermission } from '../../../../identity'
55: 
56: export const GET = list({ authorize: requirePermission('list-roles') })
57: ```
58: 
59: ```ts
60: // routes/(authenticated)/roles/detail/[id]/+server.ts
61: import { detail } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
62: import { requirePermission } from '../../../../../identity'
63: 
64: export const GET = detail({ authorize: requirePermission('detail-roles') })
65: ```
66: 
67: `list({})` and `detail({})` use the inherited entity and hooks. The empty object
68: adds no operation permission. Detail, update, and delete use `id`; set `param`
69: when the directory parameter has another name.
70: 
71: A custom HTTP action uses `defineRoute({ action, ... })`. It has no `method` or
72: `path` option:
73: 
74: ```ts
75: // routes/health/+server.ts
76: import { defineRoute } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
77: 
78: export const GET = defineRoute({ action: () => ({ ok: true }) })
79: ```
80: 
81: Keep callbacks inline when they need inferred scope types. Extract business
82: operations with explicit business inputs, not copied route-context types.
83: 
84: ## Inheritance and hooks
85: 
86: Context is created per request. Child fields replace equal parent keys. Each
87: scope's hooks retain that scope's context and identity view; a child replacement
88: does not change the parent view. Each identity resolver is memoized per request.
89: Parent authorization rejection stops child
90: context work. Error hooks unwind only through entered scopes.
91: 
92: Order: scope context and authorization, route authorization, canonical state
93: parsing, server write values, `before`, `validate`, action, operation `after`.
94: `before` and `validate` run from parent to child; `after` runs in reverse.
95: Use Hono middleware for headers, cleanup, and behavior required on all responses.
96: 
97: A new entity clears inherited record enrichment. An enrich-only scope replaces
98: the inherited converter. Canonical results pass through scope conversion, then
99: route enrichment, then the envelope. See [public records](public-records.md).
100: 
101: Keep `entity`, `enrich`, `identity`, `pipeline`, and `source` out of returned
102: business context; these keys are reserved. Use supported `state.where`
103: and `state.values` for canonical read/write constraints; arbitrary context keys
104: do not change source behavior.
````

```
1: # Execute a module
2: 
3: ## Assignment
4: 
5: For module delivery, the parent owns questions, scope, progress and review.
6: Delegate implementation and repair to one continuing worker when the harness
7: supports it. The parent must not repeat the worker's discovery or edit its files
8: in parallel. Use direct execution when delegation is unavailable, prohibited or
9: cannot preserve ownership; state that reason. Split workers only for genuinely
10: independent work with non-conflicting files and test targets.
11: 
12: An assignment names the requested result, exact owners/patterns, unresolved facts,
13: permitted writes, environment and completion check. Pass decisions, not the
14: transcript or an instruction to rediscover them. The active assignment contains
15: one usable result and its prerequisites; remaining work stays in the work record.
16: 
17: For UI delivery, include API, page, navigation, permissions and development setup
18: in the assignment. Include [DESIGN.md](../../../../DESIGN.md) and any approved
19: exceptions as required inputs for the executor and reviewer. On resume, check
20: whether these inputs changed before reusing earlier UI decisions.
21: An early API integration check can precede the UI checkpoint;
22: keep the remaining UI work in the same assignment.
23: Review the first page's source wiring and
24: non-browser assertions before repeating the pattern. Assign no E2E work.
25: 
26: Full-process work uses the [worksheet state rules](module-execution-worksheet.md#state-and-completion).
27: Standard work uses the single design record; no worksheet checker is needed. Keep work
28: with an early interface dependency in one plan when a split would block useful
29: progress or require a false completion state.
30: 
31: ## Prepare and build
32: 
33: Before implementation, check required configuration presence without exposing
34: secrets, database baseline, test commands and setup authority together. Reuse
35: current evidence. Finish this check with usable prerequisites or named blockers;
36: continue independent work while missing authority is resolved.
37: Resolve current package commands and reuse a current preflight. Select only
38: needed capabilities with `pnpm module:preflight -- --needs <capabilities>`.
39: Establish the intended development target and write authority before setup is
40: needed. Test/E2E targets and development preview are separate.
41: For a fresh trial, confirm that source, migration history and the selected
42: database belong to the same baseline. A clean Git tree does not prove this.
43: If existing tables conflict with pending migrations, stop affected writes and
44: report the mismatch. Use a confirmed disposable target or an authorized
45: reconciliation. Do not drop tables, remove applied migrations or change journal
46: entries to make a module check pass.
47: 
48: When the main function depends on an uncertain external integration, establish
49: one working path through the application input, provider call and validated
50: result before completing dependent surfaces. Use the existing application
51: structure and the [external integration checks](verification-strategy.md#external-integrations).
52: Record the result and remaining work. This checkpoint does not complete UI delivery.
53: 
54: Before migration generation, check the affected entity import structure and
55: existing data. Resolve connected-entity/audit references using the supported
56: pattern; keep schema declarations and SQL consistent. A module task does not
57: authorize a framework redesign or removal of required constraints.
58: 
59: As soon as the first viable schema and page are ready:
60: 
61: 1. Review migration SQL and identify the target. Apply pending migrations
62:    within authority using the existing migration command, not reset/refresh.
63: 2. Inspect and run the required permission/system seed within authority. Preserve
64:    existing data; demo records and account changes are not automatically required.
65: 3. Check service readiness and review the page's route, navigation and access
66:    wiring. Report its URL, migration/seed result and unfinished work before
67:    final verification. Leave the browser walkthrough to the user; do not claim
68:    rendered behavior was verified.
69: 
70: Ask early if the target or write authority is unclear. Never substitute test/E2E
71: reset commands for development setup. A remote target is not disposable merely
72: because its configuration is available. Once applied to any target, keep migration
73: history intact; use a new migration for subsequent changes.
74: 
75: After route changes, use the current supported route/type-generation command
76: before interpreting stale route names as application type errors. Resolve a
77: missing command once; do not repeatedly clear caches or rewrite declarations.
78: 
79: ## Progress and recovery
80: 
81: Use the [tight loop](verification-strategy.md#tight-loop). Report completed
82: results, material failures and blockers with the next action. Preserve full
83: output and the real command status so diagnosis does not require a rerun.
84: 
85: On interruption, inspect saved changes/results and resume the same executor.
86: Transfer only unfinished work when recovery is not possible. Stop the old
87: executor before transferring ownership. Elapsed time alone does not establish
88: failure, but an unclear result requires diagnosis before more assignments.
89: 
90: ## Review and finish
91: 
92: Return changed owners, observed results, current evidence and remaining work.
93: Use [verification strategy](verification-strategy.md#evidence-interface) for the
94: chosen path. Review the feature once unless a separate result needs independent
95: acceptance. Prefer an independent `$verify-carta-module` reviewer at completion;
96: label self-review when delegation is unavailable or the user requests direct work.
97: 
98: Review against the original request and later decisions. Fix material in-scope
99: defects without requesting new implementation approval. Ask only for changed
100: requirements, scope or write authority. Optional suggestions do not block a
101: correct result. Report failed checks and missing proof separately from defects.
102: 
103: Update the existing work record, relevant application-map entries and, only for
104: the full process, worksheet states. Report source readiness, development preview
105: and verification separately. Record time to usable preview as well as total
106: elapsed time; keep user waits and external blockers distinct.
107: 
108: After a reported defect, inspect other uses of the same faulty pattern and reopen
109: the affected review scope. Update the existing record with the repair and current
110: evidence before restoring completion. Preserve evidence that the defect and repair
111: do not affect. Include the account role and data prerequisites needed to use the
112: preview, without exposing credentials.
```

````
1: # File routing
2: 
3: Use file placement to set the URL and the rendered parent chain. Apply the
4: ordinary folder pattern to new child CRUD pages unless the required behavior
5: calls for replacement of a parent. A completed app is evidence of behavior;
6: check its route pattern against this convention before copying it.
7: 
8: ## Place the page
9: 
10: Select the visible section arrangement from [DESIGN.md](../../../../DESIGN.md)
11: first. A route file below `detail/` retains its parent, but a named child does
12: not appear on bare-parent entry by file placement alone. An `index.route.vue`
13: is the default child. Routing `Tabs` selects its first available child. The
14: router supports these mechanisms; it does not choose the app's section layout.
15: 
16: A folder adds URL segments. Its `index.route.vue` is a replaceable default
17: page. A route file beside a matching folder retains that page as a parent.
18: Give peer navigation entries sibling folders at the same URL depth, so each
19: entry path matches one section. A group landing page is one such sibling: it
20: lives in its own folder (for example `pos/sell/index.route.vue`), never as
21: the bare group `pos/index.route.vue` while its peers sit a level deeper.
22: A navigation group supplies labels
23: and order; file placement supplies URLs and parents.
24: Use `AppRouterView` in retained Carta record pages for the existing identity
25: and refresh behavior. The route validator also accepts native `RouterView`.
26: 
27: For User Detail with a Roles List, use:
28: 
29: ```text
30: users/[userId]/detail.route.vue
31: users/[userId]/detail/roles/index.route.vue
32: users/[userId]/detail/roles/[roleId]/detail.route.vue
33: ```
34: 
35: Opening Role Detail keeps User Detail and replaces Roles List. If Role Detail
36: has its own children, its matching `detail/` folder retains Role Detail too.
37: The same rule applies at each depth.
38: 
39: Use native dotted file segments when a destination must leave a matching
40: rendered parent and keep its URL segments. The containing folder sets which
41: higher parents remain. These are alternative placements for a destination:
42: 
43: | Visible result | Route file |
44: | --- | --- |
45: | Replace User Detail and its children | `users/[userId]/detail.roles.[roleId].detail.route.vue` |
46: | Keep User Detail; replace Role Detail and its children | `users/[userId]/detail/roles/[roleId]/detail.permissions.[permissionId].detail.route.vue` |
47: 
48: Keep one placement per destination. Use this file structure instead of a
49: replacement flag, route metadata switch, or a second layout system. Existing
50: sibling workflow pages can stay flat when they already give the required
51: result; they do not need dots unless a matching rendered parent must be left.
52: 
53: Preserve existing URLs and explicit route names during migration. Generated
54: names use static URL segments, including those in dotted files. Equivalent
55: nested and dotted placements get the same generated name. For a parent and
56: empty index with the same name, the index keeps the name and the parent becomes
57: unnamed. Named navigation then opens the default page.
58: 
59: Generation rejects duplicate names, duplicate page paths, layout collisions,
60: and rendered parents without an outlet. An empty index may share its parent
61: URL; a conditional outlet is valid. Correct the file structure when generation
62: fails instead of adding a second name or suppressing validation.
63: 
64: ## Navigation and page lifetime
65: 
66: Use the app routing `Tabs` with `RouteTab` named targets. Missing parameters
67: come from the current route; explicit target parameters take precedence. Tabs
68: replace bare-parent entry with the first available child. With no available
69: child, the parent stays visible. A tab stays active on detail, edit, and deeper
70: pages within its section while its owner remains matched at the same identity.
71: 
72: Use the resource's scoped collection `backTo` for page Back, including after
73: parent replacement and on direct entry. A workflow without a routed collection
74: supplies an explicit target and preserves its selection query. Browser Back
75: uses history. The URL hierarchy alone does not define the page Back target.
76: 
77: Changing a parent ID remounts that parent and its descendants through
78: `AppRouterView`. Changing a child ID keeps higher parents mounted. Query and
79: hash changes keep the current pages mounted. Reuse the existing outlet keys
80: and scoped refresh behavior.
81: 
82: File ancestry does not grant access or prove API scope. Keep route guards,
83: resource access, and API checks. Router code in `apps/web` is project-owned;
84: a change in Carta upstream does not migrate another application.
85: 
86: ## Verify changed behavior
87: 
88: Review generated URLs, names, parameters, parent outlets, tab targets and scoped
89: Back targets. Reuse existing non-browser checks for changed routing code.
90: Do not repeat framework navigation or page-lifetime tests for a normal module.
91: API checks own access enforcement. Source review does not prove visible behavior;
92: report that limit without starting browser tests or a manual journey.
````

````
# Build resource forms

Read [DESIGN.md](../../../DESIGN.md) before selecting form layout or controls,
including when this skill is used directly for a custom action.

Apply [discovery reuse](../carta-module-development/SKILL.md#discovery-reuse).
Trace the changed value through its API schema, resource and route; reuse
current pattern decisions from the plan. Read the field contract in
`packages/loom/README.md` when its shape is unresolved, and
`apps/web/src/framework/inputs/registry.ts` when renderer registration or defaults
are unresolved. Use [web-ui-surfaces](../web-ui-surfaces/SKILL.md) for changed
page composition and `docs/ui/forms.md` for an unresolved app form default.

## Define the value contract

Bind standard resources with app `defineSchema` from `@/framework/schema`.
Pass raw Zod schemas; the app seam calls `fromZod` and infers parsed types.
A Hono route or an explicit custom contract supplies the expected types.
For non-asset fields, add a local form transform only when the control and API
shapes differ.
Keep custom action schemas separate from standard CRUD schemas.

For file/image fields in standard or custom actions, read the
[asset-object contract](../carta-module-development/references/frontend-field-contract.md#asset-fields)
before selecting the write schema. Use that contract to resolve an input mismatch.

Use one `defineFields` catalog. Select only each action's fields in its required
order. A schema key string uses the app field default; a field reference adds
module behavior. One terminal `.override(...)` handles one action difference.
Keep `display.read` for display projection and `form.write` for necessary submit
conversion. Omit identity functions and copied input/output type wrappers.

For state-dependent inputs, supply the current record through form context.
Match required state and submit validation to the server predicate, including
previously retained values. Help text alone does not enforce a required input.

Account for every required write value: user input, fixed parent context, or
server-owned data. Show editable required fields. Supply fixed values through
`initialData`; keep server-owned values out of client write schemas. Do not add
hidden controls merely to satisfy a schema.

Use `form.initialValue` for a fresh omitted-key default. Loaded values and
explicit `false`, `null`, or empty values must win. The draft stores control
values; the submit copy passes through the field writer, schema, then business
validators. A failed submit must preserve the draft.

## Select controls

Custom business operations use the same framework forms and controls as CRUD.
Give the operation its own schema and action; let the form own input, validation
and pending state. Use local UI code only for a named requirement that registered
renderers and existing composites cannot meet. Record that gap in the existing
work record before implementing the exception.

Read [field choices](references/form-field-types.md) when selecting a new control
or resolving a value mismatch.
Use the registered renderer, then an existing composite. Use `table`/`TableInput`
for form-owned row arrays. If those cannot express one domain value, use the
[custom field contract](references/custom-field-contract.md).

The outer form owns label, required state, error, help, and grid span.

Use `defineFields` for component-derived prop checks. Include `form.renderer`
when overriding props so the override is checked. For separate prop objects,
use `satisfies FormRendererProps<'renderer-key'>` from
`@southneuhof/loom/renderers/formContracts`. Known props keep their
component types; extra props remain open. Broad field annotations do not prove
prop validity. Check extra prop names against the component; type checks cannot
detect those spelling errors. These checks do not validate runtime data.

Apply the [framework-first composition rule](../web-ui-surfaces/SKILL.md#framework-first-composition)
once per form pattern. Select the form surface from
[DESIGN.md](../../../DESIGN.md#actions-and-forms).
Pass the standard action bag directly. Use a `DialogForm` trigger slot without
`v-model:open` for ordinary contextual forms, and render one keyed form per
record action. Let the form own draft, validation, pending state, visibility,
and completion. Use controlled visibility only when another page control must
coordinate it. Read [the dialog form contract](../../../docs/ui/forms.md#dialog-forms)
for that advanced path.

For a custom submit, trace write success, form completion and data refresh in
order. Start later refresh work from `submitted`; keep it separate from the
write so refresh rejection reports stale data and does not retry the write.
Use the supported loading and invalidation path from
the [query-cache contract](../carta-module-development/references/web-query-cache.md).
Report a failed write separately from a failed refresh after a successful write.

## Configure relation sources

For each new or changed relation, use the
[display and form pattern](../web-ui-surfaces/references/fields.md).
Complete its API display data and list/detail projection with the form, rather
than leaving display work for a later assignment.

Use the owner resource as `source`. Its `list` action supplies server search and
paging; `detail` resolves a selected record outside the current page. Static
arrays are for closed choices, not database collections. Pass filters through
`searchParameters`; the owner endpoint owns their contract.

For a parent-dependent field:

```ts
behavior: {
  disabled: ({ draft }) => !draft.divisionId,
  props: ({ draft }) => ({ searchParameters: { divisionId: draft.divisionId } }),
  resetWhen: ({ draft }) => draft.divisionId,
},
```

Use pure synchronous behavior. `visible` controls field presence and submission;
`disabled` controls editing; `derived` calculates a non-editable value. Hidden
fields are omitted, so the schema and server must agree on conditional values.
If several dependencies can invalidate a child, the reset key must reflect
each one; a truthy `a || b` expression can hide changes to `b`.

Use `context` for stable screen information. Standard create/update actions
supply reserved `context.operation` and `context.permission`. Where the source
requires action scope, use that permission rather than a hard-coded create
permission. The server validates it; a query parameter grants no authority.

For multi lookup/select, use `selectionValues(exactItemSchema)`: keep exact
selected record objects and submit them unchanged. Do not add an ID-array
writer.

## Connect writes

Read [backend form contract](references/backend-form-contract.md) when a source
or write contract changes. Use a custom action for a distinct domain operation,
not another options endpoint. Give it only its actual input fields. Keep state
checks and atomic parent/child writes on the server. A child with independent
screens or permissions needs its own resource; a row owned by one form does not.

Continue authorized implementation choices. Ask only for a missing decision
that changes business behavior, access, or transaction semantics. A framework
package change needs explicit scope; a supported local custom field does not.

## Verify

Use [UI verification](../web-ui-surfaces/references/verification.md). Select a
check that can fail on the changed value or interaction: dependency reset,
selected-record hydration, conditional submit, row edit, or failed-save recovery.
Check server rejection of a forged relation when the write boundary changes.
Do not add tests that merely copy field order, labels, renderer names, or action
objects. Reuse existing evidence for unchanged framework behavior.

Bundled resource files (read on demand, paths relative to the base directory):
- agents/openai.yaml
- references/backend-form-contract.md
- references/custom-field-contract.md
- references/form-field-types.md
````

```
# Carta module plan

Translate an approved module contract into repository-grounded implementation
plans. Record intent, affected owners, scope, steps, checks and completion.
This skill plans the selected behavior; it does not run a general audit, choose
new product scope, or implement source changes.

## Confirm authority and current context

Start with the [standard module base](../carta-module-development/references/standard-module.md),
including custom workflows added to it.
Add exact owners, work order, setup and suitable checks to the existing work
record. Confirm that the standard design approval gate records the user's
approval of this exact revision. If it does not, return to `$carta-module-design`,
present the design and stop for approval before planning. Keep the plan in the
standard design record without creating
numbered plans, a worksheet or UI JSON. A plan-only request stops there.
Use the remaining procedure only for a scoped full contract or an existing full
plan. A custom action alone does not require it. Include workflow restrictions
on standard actions in the first result; keep later workflow work explicit.

Read the design and its approval source. Use the shared
[module contract](../carta-module-design/references/module-contract.md) to assess
readiness without requiring a rewrite into a particular layout. Keep an
existing plan that already meets the same bar.

Apply [discovery reuse](../carta-module-development/SKILL.md#discovery-reuse).
Inspect the required owners and consumers, relevant layer contracts,
and current package scripts/configuration. Record an existing exemplar for
non-obvious patterns. Separate observed repository facts from proposed technical
changes. Module delivery uses non-browser Vitest, type checking and linting; select
appropriate checks rather than asking the user to choose a testing stack.
Resolve exact commands from this checkout and distinguish script inspection
from a successful execution.

Technical discovery ends when each requested action has an exact owner, a
supported implementation path or named gap, and a suitable check. Record each
pattern decision with an exact source pointer once in the owners table.

For backend routes, read the
[file-routing contract](../api-conventions/references/file-routing.md). Name the
method exports, URL parameters, inherited scopes, and affected SDK consumers.
Keep database domains separate from HTTP routing.

For web work, apply `$web-ui-surfaces` and, for forms, `$build-resource-form`.
Read [DESIGN.md](../../../DESIGN.md) before selecting the UI structure. Link its
applicable sections in the existing plan; record only required exceptions.
Select supported interaction patterns before choosing custom routes or controls.
Map each required UI action to its entry point, inputs, access/state conditions
and visible result in the plan's existing owner rows. Reference the design's
predicates rather than copying them. Reuse pattern choices across actions; record
only actual framework gaps as exceptions.

For web route changes, read the
[file-routing convention](../web-ui-surfaces/references/file-routing.md). Map
the required visible parent chain to route files and page Back targets. Preserve
existing URLs and names unless the approved change includes them. Treat file
placement within settled behavior as a technical decision.

If planning exposes a missing business rule or a conflict with approved intent,
return that specific issue to `$carta-module-design`. Preserve unaffected work.
Make ordinary technical decisions within the design's delegated scope. A missing
implementation owner is work to plan, not itself a product blocker. Choose local
storage, symbols, permission-code spelling and transaction mechanics when behavior
is settled. Ask the decision owner only for missing business policy or authority;
name the observable outcome that the answer changes. Storage representation is
technical; who may create/read records or receive a grant is business policy.
An absent source of project assignments cannot be replaced by test fixtures and
called a complete application workflow.

## Organize the work

Put environment preparation first. Record selected capabilities and the
`module:preflight` result in the plan's environment row. Use existing setup within
task authority. Name any blocked check and its missing prerequisite.
Include development migration, required seed and preview under the
[execution setup rule](../carta-module-development/references/execution.md#prepare-and-build);
test setup does not replace them.

Select the first result under the
[assignment rule](../carta-module-development/references/execution.md#assignment).
Use the worksheet's plan dependency rule to separate plans from assignments.

Use [plan-template.md](references/plan-template.md) for numbered plans at
`plans/<feature>/001-<result>.md`. Preserve existing numbering on resume. The
complete handoff is the design, worksheet, selected plans and referenced source,
not a transcript or repeated copy of the design in each file.

Use the [worksheet contract](../carta-module-development/references/module-execution-worksheet.md)
for the dependency/status index and acceptance ownership. Map every acceptance

## Review and hand off

Check complete acceptance coverage, dependency order, actual paths and commands,
write boundaries, and design revision. Check the plan as a fresh implementer:
it must resolve what to change and how to prove it without another product
```

```
26: }

28: async function insertPermission(db: ReturnType<typeof getDb>, code: string) {
29:   await db.insert(permissions).values({ id: testId('permission'), permissionCode: code, name: code }).onConflictDoNothing()
30:   const row = (await db.select({ id: permissions.id }).from(permissions).where(eq(permissions.permissionCode, code)).limit(1))[0]
31:   if (!row) throw new Error(`Permission fixture is missing: ${code}`)
32:   return row.id
33: }

37:  * grants, registers teardown, and returns the session. Business rows the spec
38:  * creates stay the spec's responsibility.
39:  */
40: export async function createSystemSession(permissionCodes: readonly string[], label = 'test'): Promise<TestSession> {
41:   const db = getDb()
42:   const userId = testId(`${label}-user`)
43:   const roleId = testId(`${label}-role`)
44:   const email = `${userId}@example.invalid`
45: 
46:   await db.insert(users).values({ id: userId, name: `${label} Test User`, email })
47:   await db.insert(accounts).values({ id: testId(`${label}-account`), accountId: userId, providerId: 'credential', userId, password: await hashPassword(PASSWORD) })
48:   await db.insert(roles).values({ id: roleId, roleCode: testId(`${label}-role-code`), name: `${label} Test Role` })
49:   for (const code of permissionCodes) {
50:     const permissionId = await insertPermission(db, code)
51:     await db.insert(rolePermissions).values({ roleId, permissionId })
52:   }
53:   await db.insert(roleAssignments).values({ userId, roleId })
54: 
55:   const signedIn = await getAuth().api.signInEmail({ body: { email, password: PASSWORD }, returnHeaders: true })
56:   registerTeardown({ userId, roleId })
57:   return { userId, roleId, cookie: signedIn.headers.get('set-cookie')?.split(';')[0] ?? '' }
58: }
59: 
60: const teardowns: Array<() => Promise<void>> = []
61: 
62: function registerTeardown(ids: { userId: string; roleId: string }) {
63:   teardowns.push(async () => {
64:     const db = getDb()
65:     await db.delete(sessions).where(eq(sessions.userId, ids.userId))
66:     await db.delete(accounts).where(eq(accounts.userId, ids.userId))
67:     await db.delete(roleAssignments).where(eq(roleAssignments.userId, ids.userId))
68:     await db.delete(rolePermissions).where(eq(rolePermissions.roleId, ids.roleId))
69:     await db.delete(roles).where(eq(roles.id, ids.roleId))
70:     await db.delete(users).where(eq(users.id, ids.userId))
71:   })
72: }
73: 
74: /** Runs and clears every registered session teardown (use in afterEach/afterAll). */
75: export async function cleanupSessions(): Promise<void> {
76:   while (teardowns.length) await teardowns.pop()!()
77: }

79: // Session teardown must precede the pool close, so it hooks into closeDb
80: // instead of relying on spec-level hook ordering.
```

```
2: import { Pool } from 'pg'
3: import { bindDomainDatabase, defineDomainSchema } from '@southneuhof/sprindle/model'
4: import type { DomainPart } from '@southneuhof/sprindle/model'
5: import { domains } from './domains'
6: 
7: let pool: Pool | undefined
8: let db: ReturnType<typeof drizzle> | undefined
9: let domainSchema: ReturnType<typeof defineDomainSchema> | undefined
10: /** Runs registered test-session teardowns when the pool closes (test-only). */
11: let onPoolClose: (() => Promise<void>) | undefined
12: 
13: function domainParts(): readonly DomainPart[] {
14:   return domains
15: }
16: 
17: export function getDb() {
18:   const connectionString = process.env.DATABASE_URL
19:   if (!connectionString) throw new Error('DATABASE_URL is required.')
20: 
21:   if (!db) {
22:     const schema = defineDomainSchema(domainParts())
23:     pool ??= new Pool({ connectionString })
24:     db = drizzle({ client: pool, relations: schema.relations as never })
25:     bindDomainDatabase(schema, db)
26:     domainSchema = schema
27:   }
28:   return db
29: }
30: 
31: export function getDomainSchema() {
32:   getDb()
33:   return domainSchema!
34: }
35: 
36: export type Db = ReturnType<typeof getDb>
37: export type Tx = Parameters<Parameters<Db['transaction']>[0]>[0]
38: export type DbOrTx = Db | Tx
39: 
40: /** Registers teardown work that must run before the pool closes (tests only). */
41: export function setPoolCloseHook(hook: () => Promise<void>) {
42:   onPoolClose = hook
43: }
44: 
45: export async function closeDb() {
46:   if (onPoolClose) {
47:     const hook = onPoolClose
48:     onPoolClose = undefined
49:     await hook()
50:   }
51:   await pool?.end()
52:   pool = undefined
53:   db = undefined
54:   domainSchema = undefined
55: }
```

```
1: import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm'
2: import type { PermissionCode } from './authorization/catalog'
3: import { getDb } from './db'
4: import { permissions } from './routes/(authenticated)/permissions/permissions.entity'
5: import {
6:   roleAssignments,
7:   roles,
8:   rolePermissions,
9: } from './routes/(authenticated)/roles/roles.entity'
10: import { users } from './routes/(authenticated)/users/users.entity'
11: 
12: export type OrgIdentity = {
13:   userId: string
14:   user: {
15:     id: string
16:     name: string
17:     email: string
18:     statusCode: string
19:   }
20:   roleCodes: string[]
21:   permissions: ReadonlySet<PermissionCode>
22: }
23: 
24: function activeGrantCondition(userId: string, permissionCode?: PermissionCode) {
25:   return and(
26:     eq(roleAssignments.userId, userId),
27:     eq(roleAssignments.active, true),
28:     eq(users.statusCode, 'active'),
29:     eq(roles.active, true),
30:     eq(rolePermissions.active, true),
31:     eq(permissions.active, true),
32:     permissionCode ? eq(permissions.permissionCode, permissionCode) : undefined,
33:   )
34: }
35: 
36: function grantQuery() {
37:   const db = getDb()
38:   return db
39:     .select({ permissionCode: permissions.permissionCode })
40:     .from(roleAssignments)
41:     .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, roleAssignments.userId))
42:     .innerJoin(roles, eq(roles.id, roleAssignments.roleId))
43:     .innerJoin(rolePermissions, eq(rolePermissions.roleId, roles.id))
44:     .innerJoin(permissions, eq(permissions.id, rolePermissions.permissionId))
45: }
46: 
47: export async function resolveIdentity(userId: string): Promise<OrgIdentity | null> {
48:   const db = getDb()
49:   const profile = await db
50:     .select({
51:       id: users.id,
52:       name: users.name,
53:       email: users.email,
54:       statusCode: users.statusCode,
55:     })
56:     .from(users)
57:     .where(eq(users.id, userId))
58:     .limit(1)
59:   const user = profile[0]
60:   if (!user || user.statusCode !== 'active') return null
61: 
62:   const activeRoles = await db
63:     .selectDistinct({ roleCode: roles.roleCode })
64:     .from(roleAssignments)
65:     .innerJoin(roles, eq(roles.id, roleAssignments.roleId))
66:     .where(and(
67:       eq(roleAssignments.userId, userId),
68:       eq(roleAssignments.active, true),
69:       eq(roles.active, true),
70:     ))
71: 
72:   const granted = await grantQuery().where(activeGrantCondition(userId))
73:   return {
74:     userId,
75:     user,
76:     roleCodes: activeRoles.map(({ roleCode }) => roleCode),
77:     permissions: new Set(granted.map(({ permissionCode }) => permissionCode as PermissionCode)),
78:   }
79: }
80: 
81: export async function resolveEffectivePermissions(userId: string): Promise<ReadonlySet<PermissionCode>> {
82:   const identity = await resolveIdentity(userId)
83:   return identity?.permissions ?? new Set<PermissionCode>()
84: }
85: 
86: export async function can(userId: string, permissionCode: PermissionCode) {
87:   const rows = await grantQuery()
88:     .where(activeGrantCondition(userId, permissionCode))
89:     .limit(1)
90:   return Boolean(rows[0])
91: }
```

```
import { deleteRoute, HttpError, isHttpError, notFound } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
import { and, eq } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { getDb } from '../../../../../db'
import { requirePermission } from '../../../../../identity'
import { roleAssignments, roles } from '../../roles.entity'

export const DELETE = deleteRoute({
  authorize: requirePermission('delete-roles'),
  run: async ({ state }) => {
    await getDb().transaction(async (tx) => {
      const assignments = await tx
        .select({ id: roleAssignments.id })
        .from(roleAssignments)
        .where(and(eq(roleAssignments.roleId, state.id), eq(roleAssignments.active, true)))
      if (assignments.length) throw new HttpError(409, 'role_in_use', undefined, [{ field: 'assignmentCount', message: String(assignments.length) }])
      await tx.delete(roleAssignments).where(eq(roleAssignments.roleId, state.id))
      const deleted = await tx.delete(roles).where(eq(roles.id, state.id)).returning({ id: roles.id })
      if (!deleted[0]) throw notFound()
    })
  },
  error: async ({ c, error }) => {
    if (!isHttpError(error) || error.code !== 'role_in_use') return
    const assignmentCount = Number(error.issues?.find((item) => item.field === 'assignmentCount')?.message ?? 0)
    return c.json({ error: error.code, assignmentCount }, 409)
  },
})
---
import { createEntity } from '@southneuhof/sprindle/entity'
import { boolean, pgTable, primaryKey, text, timestamp, uniqueIndex } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'
import { createInsertSchema, createSelectSchema, createUpdateSchema } from 'drizzle-orm/zod'
import { permissions } from '../permissions/permissions.entity'
import { users } from '../users/users.entity'

export const auditFields = {
  createdByUserId: text('created_by_user_id').references(() => users.id),
  updatedByUserId: text('updated_by_user_id').references(() => users.id),
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at', { mode: 'string' }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at', { mode: 'string' }).notNull().defaultNow(),
}

export const roles = pgTable('roles', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey().$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
  roleCode: text('role_code').notNull().unique(),
  name: text('name').notNull(),
  description: text('description'),
  active: boolean('active').notNull().default(true),
  ...auditFields,
})

export const rolePermissions = pgTable('role_permissions', {
  roleId: text('role_id').notNull().references(() => roles.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  permissionId: text('permission_id').notNull().references(() => permissions.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' }),
  active: boolean('active').notNull().default(true),
  ...auditFields,
}, (table) => [primaryKey({ columns: [table.roleId, table.permissionId] })])

export const roleAssignments = pgTable('role_assignments', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey().$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
  userId: text('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  roleId: text('role_id').notNull().references(() => roles.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' }),
  active: boolean('active').notNull().default(true),
  ...auditFields,
}, (table) => [
  uniqueIndex('role_assignments_user_role_idx').on(table.userId, table.roleId),
])

const write = { id: true, createdByUserId: true, updatedByUserId: true, createdAt: true, updatedAt: true } as const

export const role = createEntity({
  table: roles,
  schemas: {
    create: createInsertSchema(roles).omit(write),
    update: createUpdateSchema(roles).omit(write),
    select: createSelectSchema(roles),
  },
})

```

```
import { createHonoResourceActions } from '@/framework/hono'

import { fromZod } from '@southneuhof/loom'
import type {
  CheckedSchemaIdentity,
  FormValidatorInput,
  IdentityFunction,
  IdentityKeyOf,
  InvalidSchemaIdentity,
  RecordIdentity,
  SchemaIdentityDeclaration,
  WebResourceCreateOf,
  WebResourceQueryOf,
  WebResourceRecordOf,
  WebResourceSchema,
  WebResourceSchemaBoundary,
  WebResourceUpdateOf,
} from '@southneuhof/loom'
import type { AppResourceContract, HonoCreateOf, HonoQueryOf, HonoRecordOf, HonoUpdateOf } from './hono/contracts'

type SchemaSource = Parameters<typeof fromZod>[0] & { _input: unknown; _output: object }
type SchemaOutput<TSchema> = TSchema extends { _output: infer TOutput } ? TOutput : never
type Exact<TActual, TExpected> = [TActual] extends [TExpected] ? ([TExpected] extends [TActual] ? true : false) : false
type ShapeOf<TSchema> = TSchema extends { shape: infer TShape } ? (TShape extends (...args: never[]) => infer TResult ? TResult : TShape) : never
type FieldInput<TField> = TField extends { _input: infer TInput } ? TInput : never
type RequiredKeys<TSchema> =
  ShapeOf<TSchema> extends infer TShape
    ? TShape extends Record<string, { _input: unknown }>
      ? { [TKey in keyof TShape]: undefined extends FieldInput<TShape[TKey]> ? never : TKey }[keyof TShape]
      : never
    : never
type SourceAt<TDefinition, TKey extends PropertyKey> = TDefinition extends Record<TKey, infer TSchema> ? TSchema : never
type WriteContract<TWire extends object, TSchema> = TSchema extends SchemaSource
  ? [SchemaOutput<TSchema>] extends [TWire]
    ? [RequiredKeys<TSchema>] extends [keyof TWire]
      ? TSchema
      : never
    : never
  : never

type CheckedIdentity<TRecord extends object, TDefinition> = CheckedSchemaIdentity<TRecord, TDefinition extends { identity?: infer TDeclaration } ? TDeclaration : undefined>

type Definition<TRecord extends object, TQuery extends object, TCreate extends object, TUpdate extends object, TDefinition extends object = { identity?: SchemaIdentityDeclaration<TRecord> }> = {
  identity?: TDefinition extends { identity?: infer TDeclaration }
    ? [TDeclaration] extends [IdentityKeyOf<TRecord>]
      ? TDeclaration
      : [TDeclaration] extends [readonly IdentityKeyOf<TRecord>[]]
        ? TDeclaration
        : [TDeclaration] extends [IdentityFunction<TRecord>]
          ? TDeclaration
          : SchemaIdentityDeclaration<TRecord>
    : SchemaIdentityDeclaration<TRecord>
  record?: SchemaSource
  query?: SchemaSource
  create?: SchemaSource
  update?: SchemaSource
  validators?: {
    create?: readonly FormValidatorInput<TCreate>[]
    update?: readonly FormValidatorInput<TUpdate>[]
  }
} & CheckedIdentity<TRecord, TDefinition>
type RouteDefinitionShape<TRoute> = Omit<Definition<HonoRecordOf<TRoute>, HonoQueryOf<TRoute>, HonoCreateOf<TRoute>, HonoUpdateOf<TRoute>>, 'record' | 'create' | 'update' | 'validators'> & {
  validators?: ('create' extends keyof TRoute ? { create?: readonly FormValidatorInput<HonoCreateOf<TRoute>>[] } : { create?: never }) &
    ('update' extends keyof TRoute ? { update?: readonly FormValidatorInput<HonoUpdateOf<TRoute>>[] } : { update?: never })
} & ('create' extends keyof TRoute ? { create: SchemaSource } : { create?: never }) &
  ('update' extends keyof TRoute ? { update: SchemaSource } : { update?: never })
type RouteDefinitionContract<TRoute, TDefinition extends RouteDefinitionShape<TRoute>, TRecordSchema extends SchemaSource> = {
  record: Exact<SchemaOutput<TRecordSchema>, HonoRecordOf<TRoute>> extends true ? TRecordSchema : never
} & (TDefinition extends { query: infer TQuery } ? { query: Exact<SchemaOutput<TQuery>, HonoQueryOf<TRoute>> extends true ? TQuery : never } : object) &
  ('create' extends keyof TRoute ? { create: WriteContract<HonoCreateOf<TRoute>, SourceAt<TDefinition, 'create'>> } : object) &
  ('update' extends keyof TRoute ? { update: WriteContract<HonoUpdateOf<TRoute>, SourceAt<TDefinition, 'update'>> } : object)

type CustomDefinition<TContract extends WebResourceSchemaBoundary> = {
  identity?: SchemaIdentityDeclaration<WebResourceRecordOf<TContract>>
  record?: SchemaSource & { _output: WebResourceRecordOf<TContract> }
  query?: SchemaSource & { _output: WebResourceQueryOf<TContract> }
  create?: SchemaSource & { _output: WebResourceCreateOf<TContract> }
  update?: SchemaSource & { _output: WebResourceUpdateOf<TContract> }
  validators?: {
    create?: readonly FormValidatorInput<WebResourceCreateOf<TContract>>[]
    update?: readonly FormValidatorInput<WebResourceUpdateOf<TContract>>[]
  }
}
type RuntimeDefinition = Omit<Definition<object, object, object, object>, 'identity'> & {
  identity?: string | readonly string[] | ((record: never) => RecordIdentity)
}
type OutputAt<TDefinition, TKey extends PropertyKey> = SourceAt<TDefinition, TKey> extends SchemaSource ? SchemaOutput<SourceAt<TDefinition, TKey>> : object
type IdentityAt<TDefinition> = SourceAt<TDefinition, 'identity'>
type InferredRecord<TDefinition> = SchemaOutput<SourceAt<TDefinition, 'record'>> & object
type HasRecordSource<TDefinition> = [SourceAt<TDefinition, 'record'>] extends [never]
  ? false
  : [IdentityAt<TDefinition>] extends [undefined]
    ? // With no explicit identity the record source decides: the overload
      // guard checks the `id` default through CheckedSchemaIdentity.
      true
    : [IdentityAt<TDefinition>] extends [string]
      ? [Extract<keyof InferredRecord<TDefinition>, string>] extends [never]
        ? false
        : 'id' extends Extract<keyof InferredRecord<TDefinition>, string>
          ? true
          : IdentityAt<TDefinition> extends Extract<keyof InferredRecord<TDefinition>, string>
            ? true
            : false
      : true
type InferredContract<TDefinition> = WebResourceSchema<
  OutputAt<TDefinition, 'record'>,
  OutputAt<TDefinition, 'query'>,
  OutputAt<TDefinition, 'create'>,
  OutputAt<TDefinition, 'update'>,
  RecordIdentity
>

export function defineSchema<const TRoute, const TRecordSchema extends SchemaSource, const TDefinition extends RouteDefinitionShape<TRoute>>(
  route: TRoute,
  definition: TDefinition & { record: TRecordSchema } & RouteDefinitionContract<TRoute, TDefinition, TRecordSchema>
): AppResourceContract<TRoute>
export function defineSchema<const TDefinition extends RuntimeDefinition>(
  definition: HasRecordSource<TDefinition> extends true
    ? [IdentityAt<TDefinition>] extends [undefined]
      ? TDefinition & CheckedSchemaIdentity<InferredRecord<TDefinition>, undefined>
      : [IdentityAt<TDefinition>] extends [readonly []]
        ? TDefinition & InvalidSchemaIdentity
```

```
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { hashPassword } from 'better-auth/crypto'
import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { app } from '../../../app'
import { closeDb, getDb } from '../../../db'
import { accounts, sessions } from '../../auth/auth.entity'
import { getAuth } from '../../auth/auth'
import { permissions } from '../permissions/permissions.entity'
import { rolePermissions, roles, roleAssignments } from '../roles/roles.entity'
import { users } from './users.entity'

function id(prefix: string) {
  return `user-create-test-${prefix}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`
}

async function session(withPermission: boolean, permissionCodes = ['create-users']) {
  const db = getDb()
  const userId = id(withPermission ? 'admin' : 'limited')
  const email = `${userId}@example.invalid`
  await db.insert(users).values({ id: userId, name: 'Test User', email })
  await db.insert(accounts).values({
    id: id('account'),
    accountId: userId,
    providerId: 'credential',
    userId,
    password: await hashPassword('test-password'),
  })
  let roleId: string | undefined
  if (withPermission) {
    roleId = id('role')
    await db.insert(roles).values({ id: roleId, roleCode: id('role-code'), name: 'Test Role' })
    for (const permissionCode of permissionCodes) {
      await db.insert(permissions).values({ id: `permission-${permissionCode}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, permissionCode, name: permissionCode }).onConflictDoNothing()
      const permission = await db.select({ id: permissions.id }).from(permissions).where(eq(permissions.permissionCode, permissionCode)).limit(1)
      await db.insert(rolePermissions).values({ roleId, permissionId: permission[0]!.id })
    }
    await db.insert(roleAssignments).values({ userId, roleId })
  }
  const signedIn = await getAuth().api.signInEmail({ body: { email, password: 'test-password' }, returnHeaders: true })
  return { cookie: signedIn.headers.get('set-cookie')?.split(';')[0] ?? '', roleId, userId }
}

function request(body: unknown, cookie = '') {
  return app.request('/users/create', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(cookie ? { Cookie: cookie } : {}) },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
}

  afterAll(() => closeDb())

    const response = await request({ name: 'Created User', email: `${id('created')}@example.invalid`, password: 'password-123', roleIds: [sessionState.roleId!, secondRoleId] }, sessionState.cookie)

    expect(response.status).toBe(201)

  })

    expect(response.status).toBe(400)
  })

  it('rejects duplicate emails', async () => {
    const sessionState = await session(true)
    const email = `${id('duplicate')}@example.invalid`

    expect((await request(first, sessionState.cookie)).status).toBe(201)

    expect((await request({})).status).toBe(401)
    expect((await request({}, (await session(false)).cookie)).status).toBe(403)
  })

  it('rejects duplicate, missing, and inactive initial roles before account creation', async () => {

    const inactiveRoleId = id('inactive-role')

    ]
    for (const testCase of cases) {

import { list, validationError } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
import { and, asc, countDistinct, desc, eq, getTableColumns, ilike, or, type SQL } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { getDb } from '../../../../db'
import { requirePermission } from '../../../../identity'
import { user, users } from '../users.entity'

const userColumns = getTableColumns(users) as Record<string, unknown>
const userReservedQueryKeys = new Set(['page', 'limit', 'search', 'sort', 'order'])

function equalityFilters(
  query: Record<string, unknown>,
  columns: Record<string, unknown>,
  options: { ignore?: ReadonlySet<string>; reservedKeys?: ReadonlySet<string> } = {},
): SQL[] {
  const skip = new Set([...(options.reservedKeys ?? new Set(['page', 'limit', 'search', 'sort', 'order', 'permission'])), ...(options.ignore ?? [])])
  const filters: SQL[] = []
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(query)) {
    if (skip.has(key) || value === undefined || value === '') continue
    const column = columns[key]
    if (!column) throw validationError(`Unknown query parameter "${key}".`)
    filters.push(eq(column as never, value as never))
  }
  return filters
}

function searchCondition(query: Record<string, unknown>, columns: Record<string, unknown>, searchable: readonly string[]): SQL | undefined {
  const search = typeof query.search === 'string' && query.search ? `%${query.search}%` : undefined
  if (!search) return undefined
  return or(...searchable.map((field) => ilike(columns[field] as never, search)))
}

function orderClause(query: Record<string, unknown>, columns: Record<string, unknown>, fallback: SQL[]): SQL[] {
  if (!query.sort) return fallback
  const column = columns[String(query.sort)]
  if (!column) throw validationError(`Unknown sort column "${String(query.sort)}".`)
  return [query.order === 'desc' ? desc(column as never) : asc(column as never)]
}

function listWhere(query: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const search = searchCondition(query, userColumns, ['name', 'email'])
  const conditions = [
    ...equalityFilters(query, userColumns, { reservedKeys: userReservedQueryKeys }),
    ...(search ? [search] : []),
  ]
  return conditions.length ? and(...conditions) : undefined
}

export const GET = list({
  authorize: requirePermission('list-users'),
  run: async (args) => {
    const query = args.state.query
    const where = listWhere(query)
    const page = Number(query.page)
    const limit = Number(query.limit)
    const db = getDb()
    const [rows, totalRows] = await Promise.all([
      db.selectDistinct({ user: users }).from(users).where(where).orderBy(...orderClause(query, userColumns, [asc(users.name)])).limit(limit).offset((page - 1) * limit),
      db.select({ value: countDistinct(users.id) }).from(users).where(where),
    ])
    return {
      data: rows.map(({ user: row }) => user.schemas.select.parse(row)),
      total: Number(totalRows[0]?.value ?? 0),
    }
  },
})
import { created, defineRoute, HttpError, isHttpError, unauthorized } from '@southneuhof/sprindle'
import { eq, inArray } from 'drizzle-orm'
import { getDb } from '../../../../db'
import { orgIdentity, requirePermission } from '../../../../identity'
import { createAuth } from '../../../auth/auth'
import { readJsonBody } from '../../../../request-body'
import { publicRecord } from '../../../../storage/assets'
import { roleAssignments, roles } from '../../roles/roles.entity'
import { user, users } from '../users.entity'
import { createUserSchema } from '../users.create.contract'

function initialRoleIds(roleIds: string[]) {
  const uniqueRoleIds = [...new Set(roleIds)]
  if (!uniqueRoleIds.length || uniqueRoleIds.length !== roleIds.length) throw new HttpError(422, 'roles_required')
  return uniqueRoleIds
}

async function validateInitialRoles(roleIds: string[]) {
  const uniqueRoleIds = initialRoleIds(roleIds)
  const foundRoles = await getDb().select({ id: roles.id, active: roles.active }).from(roles).where(inArray(roles.id, uniqueRoleIds))
  if (foundRoles.length !== uniqueRoleIds.length || foundRoles.some((row) => !row.active)) throw new HttpError(422, 'roles_required')
  return uniqueRoleIds
}

async function assignInitialRoles(actorUserId: string, userId: string, roleIds: string[]) {
  const uniqueRoleIds = initialRoleIds(roleIds)
  await getDb().transaction(async (tx) => {
    const foundRoles = await tx.select({ id: roles.id, active: roles.active }).from(roles).where(inArray(roles.id, uniqueRoleIds))
    if (foundRoles.length !== uniqueRoleIds.length || foundRoles.some((row) => !row.active)) throw new HttpError(422, 'roles_required')
    await tx.insert(roleAssignments).values(uniqueRoleIds.map((roleId) => ({
      userId,
      roleId,
      active: true,
      createdByUserId: actorUserId,
      updatedByUserId: actorUserId,
    })))
  })
}

export const POST = defineRoute({
  openapi: { requestBody: createUserSchema },
  authorize: requirePermission('create-users'),
  action: async (args) => {
    const input = createUserSchema.parse(await readJsonBody(args.c))
    const identity = await orgIdentity(args)
    if (!identity) throw unauthorized()
    const existing = await getDb().select({ id: users.id }).from(users).where(eq(users.email, input.email)).limit(1)
    if (existing[0]) return args.c.json({ error: 'email_exists' }, 409)

    let userId: string | undefined
    try {
      await validateInitialRoles(input.roleIds)
      const result = await createAuth({ allowSignUp: true }).api.signUpEmail({
        body: { name: input.name, email: input.email, password: input.password },
      })
      userId = result.user?.id
      if (!userId) return args.c.json({ error: 'user_create_failed' }, 422)
      const updated = await getDb().select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, userId)).limit(1)
      await assignInitialRoles(identity.userId, userId, input.roleIds)
      const createdUser = user.schemas.select.parse(updated[0] ?? result.user)
      return created(args.c, publicRecord(user.schemas.select, createdUser))
    } catch (error) {
      if (userId) await getDb().delete(users).where(eq(users.id, userId))
      if (isHttpError(error)) return args.c.json({ error: error.code, ...(error.message ? { message: error.message } : {}) }, error.status as 400)
      return args.c.json({ error: 'user_create_failed' }, 409)
    }
  },
})
```
